newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia heading for minority government.
newsitem.headline: Estonia heading for minority government.

text.p: The small Baltic state of Estonia was heading for a minority government on Thursday after Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi failed to find new coalition partners.

Vaehi's Coalition Party and his allies from a bloc of small rural parties agreed late on Thursday that Vaehi should aim for a minority government after the two parties he had invited into the coalition refused to work with each other.
Vaehi was forced to try to form what will be Estonia's seventh government since it regained independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991 after his junior coalition partner quit last week.
Vaehi can command 41 seats in Estonia's fractious 101-seat parliament and hopes to count on the support of some of the centrist and left-leaning parties.
A spokeswoman for Vaehi said he was now in talks on filling the six ministerial posts abandoned by his former partners.
"He has several candidates to nearly all the posts and now he is trying to find the best and the ones most acceptable to the opposition," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
She said that Vaehi was optimistic for the support of some of the opposition parties as they did not want early elections.
She said Vaehi has already asked Estonia's ambassador to the United States, Toomas Ilves, to be foreign minister.
